comments.note: mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (hasCycle): The BFS cycle detector can only catch forward-reference cycles — e.g., new WP-X depends on WP-A, which already lists WP-X in its dependency chain. It cannot detect cycles among freshly created WPs that don't yet exist in allWps. This is the correct behavior for sequential creation workflows, but worth documenting: hasCycle is a forward-reference guard, not a general-purpose cycle detector for in-flight batch creation.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (createWorkPackage step 5): acceptance_criteria whitespace validation iterates the array and throws on first invalid criterion, but the error message does not indicate which criterion (index or value) was rejected. Low impact but a debug-quality improvement would be to include the index: 'Acceptance criteria[2] cannot be empty or whitespace-only.'

summary: Reviewed hasCycle BFS implementation, createWorkPackage guard ordering, assigned_to:null enforcement, blocked_by conditional assignment, and acceptance_criteria whitespace validation.
No blocking issues found. All five acceptance criteria verified through code reading and cross-checking with tests.
Guard ordering is correct: dependency existence (step 3) precedes cycle detection (step 3b) to prevent hasCycle from traversing unknown IDs that could cause silent misses.
unmetDeps[0] approach for blocked_by is consistent with single-blocker schema design; non-blocking improvement noted.

comments.note: mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (line 200, hasCycle): The BFS traversal is clean, pure, and correctly placed at module scope. The visited Set prevents infinite loops on pre-existing cycles in the DAG. One edge case: hasCycle traverses WorkPackageSummary.dependencies from the stored root index, so if a prior WP was seeded with a forward-reference dependency (e.g. WP-001 depends on not-yet-created WP-003), hasCycle will follow that edge. This is the correct and intended behavior for the A→B→A cycle test, but worth documenting: the function trusts that allWps is the current root index state.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (line 309, blocked_by assignment): blocked_by.blocking_work_package is set to unmetDeps[0] — only the first unmet dependency is recorded. When multiple deps are incomplete, only one appears in the blocker context. This matches the single-blocker design of the Blocker schema but could leave agents confused when there are N>1 unmet deps. A future enhancement could use description to list all unmet deps, e.g. 'Unmet deps: WP-001, WP-003'.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (step 5, acceptance_criteria validation): criterion.trim() correctly handles all whitespace types. The error message does not include the failing criterion index. QA flagged this; no further action required unless debugging DX becomes a concern.
